mechanism: Deribit dominates BTC/ETH options open interest and its weekly contracts settle Friday 08:00 UTC. Into expiry, option market makers who are net short gamma near the largest at-the-money strikes must continuously delta-hedge (buy dips / sell rallies), which mechanically pins spot in a tight range — realized vol compresses relative to its longer-term baseline. The instant those contracts settle, that hedging flow vanishes: gamma-driven suppression is removed in one discrete step, and whichever direction spot breaks in the expiry hour tends to keep going because there is no more dealer flow leaning against it. The forced, price-insensitive counterparty is the option market maker's delta-hedging desk, not a discretionary trader — they must transact regardless of view, and once their book clears they stop.
counterparty: Deribit BTC/ETH option market makers (dealers) forced to delta-hedge net-short-gamma inventory into the weekly Friday 08:00 UTC expiry; the hedging flow is price-insensitive and disappears the instant the contracts settle, which is the forcing function, not a discretionary view.
prediction: On weeks where realized vol has compressed into the Friday 08:00 UTC (Deribit weekly options expiry) bar relative to its 48h baseline, and price breaks by more than 15bps within that expiry bar, BTC/ETH will continue moving in the breakout direction over the following ~1-2 days (48 1h bars) at a net-of-cost win rate above fee_math.p_star for the registered tp_bps, because the gamma-hedging pressure that was pinning price is mechanically removed at settlement.

evidence: Glassnode's gamma-exposure primer (fetched directly) states that in positive-gamma zones 'dealers typically buy on dips and sell on rallies, which dampens volatility,' while in negative-gamma zones hedging flows 'amplify price moves,' and defines the 'gamma flip' as the level where net dealer GEX crosses zero — the transition from a pinned/mean-reverting regime to a momentum-driven one. The academic paper 'Bitcoin option expiration, gamma exposure, and intraday price reversals' (ScienceDirect, summarized via WebSearch) documents a statistically and economically significant BTC spot return reversal around Deribit options expiration, concentrated on days with elevated at-the-money open interest and strongest when cumulative gamma exposure is negative — consistent with positive-feedback hedging by dealers short gamma — and estimates the associated wealth transfer at roughly USD 50 million per annum. Blockworks reporting (via WebSearch) on a Deribit quarterly expiry states settlement can clear on the order of 45% of total active BTC options open interest in a single session, i.e. a discrete, large removal of hedging-driven flow at a known timestamp.

signal_py:
"""vol_structure_expiry_unclamp signal: post-Deribit-weekly-expiry directional continuation.
Closed bars only — all statistics are backward-looking rolling windows computed on
the bar's own close; no shift(-k), no future index use.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

RV_SHORT_WINDOW = 6      # bars (hours) — short realized-vol window
RV_LONG_WINDOW = 48      # bars (hours) — baseline realized-vol window
COMPRESSION_RATIO = 0.7  # rv_short / rv_long below this = pinned pre-expiry
BREAK_THRESHOLD = 0.0015 # 15 bps intrabar move required to count as a break


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    close = df["close"]
    open_ = df["open"]

    ret = close.pct_change()
    rv_short = ret.rolling(RV_SHORT_WINDOW).std()
    rv_long = ret.rolling(RV_LONG_WINDOW).std()
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        compression = (rv_short / rv_long) < COMPRESSION_RATIO
    compression = compression.fillna(False)

    bar_ret = (close - open_) / open_

    is_expiry_bar = (df.index.dayofweek == 4) & (df.index.hour == 8)
    is_expiry_bar = pd.Series(is_expiry_bar, index=df.index)

    fires = is_expiry_bar & compression & (bar_ret.abs() > BREAK_THRESHOLD)

    direction = np.sign(bar_ret)
    sig = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    sig[fires] = direction[fires].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return sig
